title: New Glasses Won't Fix This

patient.name: Mdm Fatimah binte Salleh
patient.presenting_complaint: Blurred vision in the left eye that new spectacles did not improve

history.hpc: Mdm Fatimah changed her glasses two months ago hoping to see better, but the left eye is still blurred. She says: 'I thought maybe need change glasses only, but new glasses also cannot help leh.' The blur is gradual and painless, with some glare in bright sunlight. No flashes, no floaters, no eye pain. She wants to know why new glasses did not work.
history.social_hx: Lives with her son's family. Enjoys reading and sewing. Non-smoker.

va.left: 6/36 with current glasses, no improvement with pinhole

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Left eye: central lens opacity (cataract). Right eye: early lens changes. Cornea clear, no redness both eyes.
examination_findings.fundus: Left fundus hazy view due to lens opacity; right fundus to be assessed by doctor

investigations.va_distance: Modified LogMAR with habitual correction: RE 6/9, LE 6/36. As LE VA was worse than 6/12, pinhole was applied — there was NO improvement, suggesting the reduced vision is not due to refractive error.
investigations.pinhole: LE: no improvement with pinhole (key finding pointing away from a refractive cause).
investigations.iop_nct: RE 17 mmHg, LE 18 mmHg — normal range.

diagnosis: Reduced left-eye vision due to a media opacity (cataract), not refractive error — explaining why new spectacles did not help. The absence of pinhole improvement is the key clue. For doctor review and cataract assessment.

immediate: Test distance VA with the patient's current (habitual) correction in place, right eye first
Apply pinhole to the left eye because VA is reduced, and carefully document that there is NO improvement
Explain that pinhole helps tell whether blur is from glasses power or from inside the eye
Perform NCT for IOP in both eyes
Maintain hand hygiene and alcohol-wipe the occluder before and after
Document VA, pinhole result, and IOP clearly for the doctor
follow_up: Doctor to examine the lens and confirm cataract
If cataract surgery is considered, refer for biometry for IOL power calculation
Review the right eye's early lens changes over time
patient_education: Explain simply that new glasses cannot fix this because the blur is from a cloudy lens (cataract), not the glasses power
Reassure her that cataract is common and can be treated with surgery
Explain the pinhole test result in lay terms — it pointed to a problem inside the eye, not the glasses
Outline next steps: doctor review and possible surgery work-up

key_points: Establishes that recently changed glasses did not improve the vision
Confirms the blur is gradual, painless, with glare and no flashes/floaters
Asks about family history (mother had cataract) and relevant systemic history
Clarifies the patient's concern (why new glasses did not help)
Tests VA with habitual correction, right eye first, with proper hygiene
Applies pinhole to the reduced eye and correctly documents NO improvement
Understands that pinhole distinguishes refractive from non-refractive causes
Performs and documents NCT for IOP in both eyes
Recognises that absence of pinhole improvement points away from a refractive cause
Links the central lens opacity to the reduced left-eye vision
Explains why new spectacles did not help (media opacity, not glasses power)
Defers confirmation of cataract and management to the doctor
Documents VA, pinhole result, and IOP accurately
Explains the pinhole result and the likely cause to the patient in simple terms
Reassures the patient and addresses her specific concern
Hands over to the doctor with a clear summary and outlines next steps
